walkthroughs.body_html:
Approaches to Research — a core area of Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Approaches to Research brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Approaches to Research.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Braun and Clarke's 2006 thematic analysis has how many phases?
Reflecting on how the researcher shapes the data is called:
options: Triangulation
Reflexivity
Coding
Saturation

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.
The sensory register.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.

mcqs.q: What is the capacity of short-term memory according to Miller?
options: Unlimited.
7 plus or minus 2 seconds.
7 plus or minus 2 items (chunks).
Because brain scans are unreliable.

mcqs.q: Which component handles visual and spatial information?
options: Because brain scans are unreliable.
The sensory register.
The visuospatial sketchpad.
The phonological loop.
